name: Bimhal
overview: Bimhal was a male member of the tribe of Asher, identified in Scripture as the son of Japhlet. His mention is brief, with no additional notes or significant narrative attached beyond his lineage. This positions him within the genealogical records that trace the descendants of the tribes of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Bimhal means 'son of circumcision,' reflecting a Hebrew origin and possibly indicating a cultural or religious significance related to the covenant of circumcision. This proper name is not noted as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Bimhal is explicitly recorded as the son of Japhlet, establishing his immediate paternal lineage. No other family relationships are documented in Scripture for him beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Bimhal's significance lies primarily in his inclusion in the genealogical records of the tribe of Asher, which serve to preserve the heritage and continuity of God's chosen people. His mention underscores the biblical emphasis on lineage and tribal identity within the covenant community. While not prominent in narrative events, his record contributes to the integrity of the biblical genealogies.
